choices.C: Management's high-level security expectations, rules, and responsibilities

questions.explanation: Security policies define the high-level security expectations and rules that procedures then implement.

questions.stem: Which is NOT one of the five NIST CSF core functions?
questions.explanation: The five NIST CSF functions are Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover. Encryption is a control within Protect.

choices.C: How employees may use organisational IT resources

questions.explanation: An AUP defines permitted and prohibited uses of organisational technology by employees.

choices.A: The broadest useful access for efficiency
choices.B: Only the minimum access needed for their specific job duties
choices.C: Shared admin credentials among trusted staff
choices.D: The weakest authentication that meets compliance

questions.explanation: Least privilege restricts access to the minimum necessary, limiting damage from compromised accounts or insider threats.

choices.B: No single person has complete control over a critical process
choices.C: All admin tasks require physical presence
choices.D: Employees rotate roles every six months

questions.explanation: Separation of duties divides critical tasks so fraud requires collusion, no individual can complete a harmful action alone.

questions.stem: Risk remaining after all planned controls are applied is:
questions.explanation: Residual risk remains after controls reduce inherent risk. Organisations accept, transfer, or further mitigate it.

choices.C: Risk-proportionate protection with controls appropriate to each sensitivity level

questions.explanation: Classification assigns sensitivity levels so proportionate controls are applied to each data category.

choices.C: Step-by-step procedures for a specific incident type

questions.explanation: Playbooks give specific step-by-step instructions for defined incident types, implementing the broader IR policy.

choices.A: Backing up data after every transaction
choices.B: Encrypting all data regardless of classification
choices.C: Taking reasonable precautions proportionate to identified risks

questions.explanation: Due care means reasonable proportionate precautions, the legal and regulatory baseline for cybersecurity obligations.

questions.stem: The NIST CSF Protect function focuses on:

choices.B: Developing safeguards to deliver critical infrastructure services

questions.explanation: Protect develops and implements safeguards: access control, training, data security, maintenance, and protective technology.
